title: A signed-in oauth2 caller lists their project sessions, revokes one, and revokes all others
asA: operator signed in through an OAuth2 provider on two browsers
iWant: to list every active project session, terminate any one of them, and terminate every one except the current in a single call
soThat: I end a stolen or forgotten session without touching the provider's admin surface

acceptanceCriteria.description: A `list()` call from an authenticated caller returns one row per active project session, each row shaped per `TAC-1003-security-auth-clerk-session-verifier.interfaces.sessionInventory` `SessionRow`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller with two active project sessions S1 (current) and S2, both issued through provider `google`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the return is exactly two rows shaped per the ownerRef interface, one with `currentSession=true` for S1 and one with `currentSession=false` for S2

acceptanceCriteria.description: `revoke(sessionId)` on a non-current session invalidates it in the session-record store; a replay from the revoked browser is treated as unauthenticated.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the current browser calls `sessionInventory.revoke("S2")` and browser B replays its next request
acceptanceCriteria.then: the revoke returns successfully; the session-record store no longer holds a record for S2; browser B is refused as unauthenticated on the next request; the audit sink records exactly one `oauth2.session_inventory_revoked` event with `{ operation, sessionIdPrefix, at }` and no other cookie- or token-carrying field

acceptanceCriteria.description: `revokeAllExceptCurrent()` invalidates every active project session for the caller other than the current one; the refresh-token chain for each revoked session is cleared alongside per REQ-007.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller with sessions S1 (current), S2, S3 and stored refresh-token chains for each
acceptanceCriteria.then: the return value is `2`; a subsequent `list()` returns exactly one row for S1; the refresh-token store no longer holds chains for S2 or S3

acceptanceCriteria.description: An unauthenticated call to any `sessionInventory` operation refuses with `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNAUTHENTICATED` and no side effect.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request with no verified session cookie
acceptanceCriteria.when: any of the three operations is invoked
acceptanceCriteria.then: each call throws `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNAUTHENTICATED`; the session-record store is unchanged; the audit sink records exactly one `oauth2.session_inventory_unauthenticated` event

acceptanceCriteria.description: `revoke(sessionId)` against a session id the caller does not own, or a session already invalidated, refuses without a side effect.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated caller and a `sessionId` naming a session belonging to a different principal or already invalidated
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call throws `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNKNOWN_SESSION`; the session-record store is unchanged; the audit sink records exactly one `oauth2.session_inventory_unknown_session` event
